title: When We Treat What We Do as a Craft
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article explores what changes when people reframe their work as a 'craft' rather than a job. Craftspeople are described as motivated primarily by personal gratification and self-respect rather than external rewards, which leads them to obsess over every detail of their process in pursuit of mastery. The author argues this mindset produces both higher-quality output and a deeper sense of life satisfaction, since craftspeople start finding connections between their work and other parts of their lives. Not everyone has the patience or intensity for this orientation, but the piece suggests the best leaders actively cultivate it, first by promoting lifelong learning and then by explicitly inviting people to think of their work as a craft. The closing observation is that a single well-chosen word, like 'craft,' can meaningfully shift how people relate to their work.
points: Treating work as a craft shifts motivation from external rewards to personal mastery and self-respect
Craftspeople obsess over every detail of process, not just the final outcome
This mindset tends to produce both higher-quality work and greater life satisfaction
Leaders can cultivate the mindset by explicitly inviting people to see their work as a craft
quotes: The pride and satisfaction people experience from doing a job well is etched deep into the human psyche.
They strive to excel for the personal gratification and self-respect they experience, not for the material or social rewards associated with the outcome.
For these lucky few, the desire to create mastery over their work becomes a lifelong obsession.
Mastery, for a craftsperson, is accomplished at every step and with every ingredient.
Not surprisingly, those who think of their work as a craft generally produce higher-quality work.
Great leaders know the power of symbolic words and images. Craft is one of those words.
